# Mortgage overpayment

Nationwide, account ending 4471-09. 2-year fix at 4.69% from 1 June 2024 to 31 May 2026. Balance on 1 Feb 2025: £186,240. Term remaining 21 years 4 months.

## The allowance

Nationwide lets me overpay up to **10% of the balance per year** of the fixed period without an early repayment charge. The year runs from the anniversary of the product, not the tax year (I got this wrong at first). 10% of the June 2024 balance (£191,880) = £19,188 per product year. ERC above that is 2% this year, 1% next.

## What I'm doing

- £400 a month by standing order, starting 1 March 2025, now that the [[Emergency fund]] is full
- Reference on the payment must be the account number plus "OP", otherwise it sits as an advance monthly payment rather than knocking down the balance. Phoned to check on 12 Feb, spoke to Dawn, call ref NW-55302
- Asked for **reduce term**, not reduce payment. Payment stays £1,126.40

## Rough sums

£400 a month at 4.69% saves about £31,900 interest over the life and takes roughly 5 years 2 months off. Calculator on the Nationwide site agrees within £200 with my own sheet, which is reassuring.

Versus putting the same £400 into the ISA: expected return maybe 6 to 7% but not guaranteed. The 4.69% is a sure thing and it's after tax. Splitting the difference is tempting. For now it's all overpaying until the remortgage, because the lower LTV will get a better rate: we're at 62% LTV, and 60% opens the next band at most lenders.

## Not this one

The flat's buy-to-let mortgage (interest only, Paragon, 5.24%) is NOT being overpaid. The interest there gets only a 20% tax credit, see [[Rental income tax]]. Still, it's the expensive one. Revisit when that fix ends in Sept 2026.

Budget line for it in [[Budget spreadsheet]].
